signature.name: War Remnants Museum
signature.detail: A powerful museum documenting the Vietnam War through photographs, military equipment and personal accounts. It is one of the city's most visited sights and offers a sobering perspective on modern history. Tip: visit early in the morning to avoid crowds and heat; tickets are inexpensive.

signature.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
signature.detail: An extensive network of underground tunnels used during the war, now a popular historical site where you can crawl through sections and learn about guerrilla tactics. It's a must-see for history buffs. Tip: go early to beat the heat and crowds; wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

signature.name: Notre Dame Cathedral of Saigon
signature.detail: A beautiful French colonial cathedral in the heart of the city, though currently under renovation. Its distinctive red bricks and twin towers make it a iconic landmark. Tip: check if interior visits are allowed; exterior viewing is still worthwhile, and it's free.

signature.name: Independence Palace
signature.detail: The former presidential palace, famous for the tank crashing through its gates in 1975, marking the end of the war. The preserved rooms and bunkers offer a fascinating glimpse into history. Tip: rent an audio guide for context; go early to avoid tour groups.

signature.name: Saigon Central Post Office
signature.detail: A stunning example of French colonial architecture, still functioning as a post office. Its vaulted ceilings and old maps make it a photographer's delight. Tip: visit during opening hours and send a postcard for a unique souvenir.

signature.name: Ben Thanh Market
signature.detail: The city's most famous market, offering everything from souvenirs to local snacks. It's a great place to experience the bustling atmosphere and practice bargaining. Tip: visit early morning for fewer crowds and fresher food; bargain hard.

transport: Taxis and ride-hailing cheap; motorbike taxis from $1-2 for short trips
